About these figures

A typical air fryer uses about 1,500 watts (800–2,000W depending on the model). Used for 25 minutes per use, 5 uses a week, it costs about 13p per use and £34.22 a year at the current price cap rate.

Worth knowing: Element cycles once hot

Source for the typical figure: Typical range (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Don't preheat longer than the recipe needs, because most models are hot in 2–3 minutes.
  • Cook in batches back to back while it's already hot.
  • Larger baskets aren't less efficient as long as you fill them.

Questions

How much does it cost to run an air fryer per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 1500W model costs about 32p an hour, allowing for it running at full power about 80% of the time.

How much does it cost to run an air fryer per year?

About £34.22 a year, based on 25 minutes per use, 5 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my air fryer's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
